memory_block.body: Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition; note when citing it.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

answer.rationale: The two measured deteriorations are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), so the funnel-repair levers are better matched to observed damage than a price response. memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer signup fields lifts first-week SMB activation) are two independently consolidated records pointing the same direction, and onboarding completion sits upstream of activation, so a single onboarding experiment plausibly addresses both declines with one slot. I verify memory_86 because it is the memory I intend to act on and its effect size drives the sizing decision. I verify memory_73 because promotional_pricing is the emotionally obvious answer to the competitor's entry pricing and it carries an explicit self-flagged defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, meaning the 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact of cohort mixing rather than a real effect. Committing the only slot this week to a discount program on the strength of a known-contaminated readout is the main failure mode available to me, so I spend budget to close it rather than to confirm something I am not planning to do. Discounting also cuts against the primary objective directly, since price cuts buy acquisition volume at the cost of per-account revenue quality and can anchor a segment to a lower willingness to pay; that is acquisition bought against sustainable qualified revenue. Downstream risk I am flagging rather than ignoring: memory_31's mechanism is cutting required fields, and memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted demo path. Fields removed at signup are exactly the qualification signal that routing and pipeline scoring consume, so an onboarding simplification that improves SMB activation could quietly degrade enterprise lead quality and downstream conversion. I therefore scope the test to the self-serve SMB path only, leave the demo-request path untouched, and instrument enterprise routing quality as a guardrail metric alongside the activation and completion primaries. Uncertainty I am not resolving: memory_86 and memory_31 are day 52 and day 12, and the current declines may be driven by the competitor's launch shifting traffic mix rather than by onboarding friction itself, in which case a friction fix will underdeliver. All inherited records are consolidated summaries with archived sources, so effect sizes are directional rather than reliable magnitudes. Standard experiment scale with a proper holdout, not a broad rollout, since I am treating the memory as a prior to be retested and not as a settled result.
